text_to_speech: (upbeat music) - Recently I completed the Master of Science in Informatics at San Jose State University. It was my first fully online program. The professor has actually made the transition very seamless for me. They're very flexible and they're actually easy to contact whenever I have questions or I need to request for an extension for an assignment or a paper. My cohort was very diverse. Some were clinicians. They have healthcare backgrounds and some were purely IT professionals. I think their demand for the informaticists will continue to grow. As Information Technology becomes more integrated with the healthcare industry, there is going to be an increase in the demand for clinicians with a background in IT. (upbeat music)

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Recently I completed the Master of Science in Informatics at San Jose State University.
It was my first fully online program.
The professors actually made the transition very seamless for me.
They're very flexible and they're actually easy to contact whenever I have questions
or I need to request for an extension for an assignment or a paper.
Some were clinicians, they have health care backgrounds and some were purely IT professionals.
I think the demand for the informatics will continue to grow as information technology
becomes more integrated with the healthcare industry.
There is going to be an increase in the demand for clinicians with a background in IT.

youtube_description: The MS in informatics program at San Jose State University was the first fully online program for Marco Oliver Lopez, '20 MS in Informatics. "I'm normally used to being able to interact with my peers and professors face-to-face, but the professors actually made the transition very seamless for me." Marco "really enjoyed" the Informatics program, as well as his "very diverse" cohort.
youtube_title: Professors Made Transition to Online Learning 'Seamless' Says Alumnus
